Claims that Senator Chuck Schumer was caught on a hot mic plotting to “blame Republicans and MAGA” for reform delays are **false**. 

According to [PolitiFact](https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2024/mar/01/instagram-posts/schumer-biden-discussed-election-not-blaming-repub/), a video circulating on social media with subtitles claiming Schumer discussed delaying reforms and blaming Republicans was altered. The original video, from October 2022, captured a conversation between Schumer and President Biden discussing the 2022 midterm elections. News coverage at the time confirmed this, with reports from [The Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/politics/watch-schumer-says-democrats-are-going-downhill-in-georgia-on-hot-mic-ff5a64a4), [The New York Post](https://nypost.com/2022/10/28/schumer-caught-on-hot-mic-telling-biden-dems-are-in-danger-going-downhill-in-georgia-senate-race/), [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2022/10/27/us/politics/schumer-caught-on-mic-forecasting-democrats-midterm-races.html), and [The Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/schumer-biden-georgia-senate-race-a924e3f24cf90d7f976542a7f9668a8c) corroborating this account. 

More recently, reporting from [CNN Politics](https://us.cnn.com/2025/11/11/politics/schumer-senate-shutdown-democrats) and [The Hill](https://digital-staging.thehill.com/homenews/senate/5601180-schumer-democrats-leadership-shutdown/) focuses on Schumer’s role in recent government funding negotiations and the resulting frustrations within the Democratic party, but does not reference any such hot mic incident.
